english: Four distinct balls are placed in three distinct boxes, each box being allowed to remain empty. The number of placements in which at least two of the boxes contain the same number of balls (an empty box contains 0 balls) is ______.
hindi: चार भिन्न गेंदों को तीन भिन्न डिब्बों में रखा जाता है, प्रत्येक डिब्बे को रिक्त रहने की अनुमति है। उन व्यवस्थाओं की संख्या, जिनमें कम से कम दो डिब्बों में गेंदों की संख्या समान है (रिक्त डिब्बे में 0 गेंदें हैं), ______ है।
solution: Complement: three different counts adding to 4 $\Rightarrow\{0,1,3\}$ only
Counts to boxes: $3!=6$; balls into groups of sizes $3,1,0$: $\dfrac{4!}{3!\,1!\,0!}=4$ $\Rightarrow 24$
solution_full: Each ball can go into any of the 3 boxes, so there are $3^{4}=81$ placements.

Complementary counting: count the placements in which the three boxes contain three different numbers of balls. Three different non-negative integers with sum 4 must be $0,1,3$ (since $0+1+2=3<4$ and any other choice with a 2 or a 4 exceeds 4 or repeats).

Assign the counts $0,1,3$ to the three distinct boxes: $3!=6$ ways. Divide the 4 distinct balls into groups of unequal sizes 3, 1, 0: $\dfrac{4!}{3!\,1!\,0!}=4$ ways. So $6\cdot4=24$ placements have all counts different.

Direct check by patterns with a repeated count: $(2,1,1)$: 3 choices of the box with 2, then $\binom{4}{2}\cdot2!=12$: $36$; $(2,2,0)$: 3 choices of the empty box, then $\binom{4}{2}=6$: $18$; $(4,0,0)$: $3$. Total $36+18+3=57$.
originality_note: New: placements of distinct balls into distinct boxes (empty allowed) classified by whether two boxes have equal counts; the complement is a single unequal-size pattern 0, 1, 3, while the direct count needs the equal-size patterns with their own corrections (way 5: three concepts in one count). Closest known: 'distribute n distinct balls into k boxes: k^n; with no box empty: onto count'. Different because: the condition is on the multiset of box sizes, including zero.
blueprint_concepts: Division into groups: equal group sizes
Division into groups: unequal group sizes
Distribution of distinct objects into distinct boxes (empty allowed / not)

concept_use.Division into groups: equal group sizes: The equal-size patterns (2,2,0) and (2,1,1) (and (4,0,0)) appear in the direct check, where groups of equal size need the usual care.
concept_use.Division into groups: unequal group size: The complement pattern 0, 1, 3 is a division into groups of unequal sizes, 4!/(3! 1! 0!) = 4, then assigned to boxes in 3! ways.
concept_use.Distribution of distinct objects into di: Distribution of distinct balls into distinct boxes with empty boxes allowed: 3^4 = 81.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and object is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed by an independent brute-force enumeration in Python (sympy/itertools), is unique and matches the Answer Plan. Checked by enumerating all 81 placements (57 with a repeated count), that the parenthesis makes two empty boxes count as equal, and that 57 is a positive 2-digit integer as planned. Changed: added '(an empty box contains 0 balls)' after the web check showed the reading 54 is possible without it.
key_step: Complementary counting: the only all-different pattern is 0, 1, 3.
justification: Two ideas (complement and size patterns with equal/unequal groups); easy to miss a pattern in a direct count. Level 3, comparable to 2026-P1-Q11 (L3).
